one_liner: Staff a Senate press gallery: credential reporters, track floor votes and legislation, brief journalists, and run media logistics for hearings and major Capitol events.
fit_summary: Daniel's knowledge of Congress and his people-oriented style fit the core of this job: briefing reporters and explaining floor and committee activity. His resume shows writing and coordination under pressure (vaccination-site logistics, leading the exercise SimCell, meeting minutes), but no media relations or Hill experience, so lead with any press, outreach or event work he has.
eligibility: Open to the public, so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed. This is a Legislative Branch (Senate Sergeant at Arms) job, and you apply through the Senate Career Page (sen.gov/1VNZQ), not USAJOBS.
A bachelor's degree is required. His M.A. (George Mason, 2016) implies one; list both degrees.
At least two years of relevant experience is required. Show how your IEM role and any other work count toward it.
No security clearance is required. Senate employment typically includes background checks, so expect one.
Applications close at 11:59pm EST on November 5, 2026, and late applications are not accepted.
strategy: Apply on the Senate Career Page by Nov 5, 2026. Senate applications are not governed by the OPM two-page USAJOBS rule, but a tight two-page resume is still smart. Follow any page or document instructions on the Senate posting.

Frame your IEM work around transferable duties you actually performed: coordinating among government agencies, briefing stakeholders, supporting time-sensitive operations or exercises, and tracking documentation.

Make your Congressional knowledge concrete. Name specific procedures you understand, such as cloture, the reconciliation process, unanimous consent, and committee jurisdiction, and cite any coursework, internships, campaigns, or advocacy that show it.
Expect a skills assessment, likely a written legislative summary or a briefing exercise. Practice by writing 150-word summaries of real Senate votes and floor action.
Use your cover letter, if accepted, to highlight event logistics and public-facing work. Also state that you are willing to work long hours, nights, weekends, and during shutdowns.
resume_bullets: Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients, in person and virtually (2022–2024).
Handled conference supplies, deliveries and office security for IEM's office (2019–2024).
Took minutes at a large travel company's weekly meetings (Feb – Aug 2024).
interview_questions: Walk us through how a bill moves from committee to final Senate passage, including how floor time is scheduled.
A network crew shows up to a hearing without credentials and space is full. What do you do?
Describe a time you managed multiple urgent priorities during a high-pressure event.
How would you brief a reporter on a significant vote in under two minutes?
watch_outs: Lack of direct media relations or Hill experience may weigh against you with the panel, so surface any relevant exposure you have.
The job is fully on-site in DC with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
It is an essential and excepted position, so expect long hours, standing, nights, weekends, and work during shutdowns.
The application window is short (Oct 22 to Nov 5, 2026), and the full announcement is hosted off USAJOBS.
